title: Goubko's BFS-tree conjecture for terminal distance spectral radius
statement: Let $\mathbf{d}$ be a tree degree sequence, and let $BFS(\mathbf{d})$ denote its breadth-first-search (greedy) tree. For a graph $G$, let $RD(G)$ be its terminal distance matrix, and let the **terminal distance spectral radius** be the spectral radius of $RD(G)$. The **BFS-tree conjecture for terminal distance spectral radius.** The tree $BFS(\mathbf{d})$ has the minimum terminal distance spectral radius among all trees with degree sequence $\mathbf{d}$. The paper establishes lower and upper bounds whose relative gap is numerically at most $3\%$, but the exact minimum statement remains open.
source_name: Mikhail Goubko, “On Minimum Terminal Distance Spectral Radius of Trees with Given Degree Sequence”, arXiv:1507.01733 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.01733

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).
